function.name: get_current_time
function.description: Get the current date, time, weekday and time zone. Call this FIRST whenever the user says anything relative such as tomorrow, tonight, next Friday or in two hours. You have no clock of your own and will otherwise guess the date wrongly.

function.name: find_contact
function.description: Look up a person in the user's contacts and return their phone numbers and email addresses. Call this before send_message, place_call or send_email whenever you were given a name rather than a number, so you send to the right person.

name.description: A name, partial name or saved nickname to search for.

function.name: remember_person_alias
function.description: Record that a nickname refers to a specific contact, for example that 'mum' means 'Jane Wilson'. Use this after the user tells you who a nickname refers to, so you never have to ask again.

alias.description: The nickname the user says, such as mum, dad, or the boss.

contact_name.description: The full contact name the nickname refers to.

function.name: send_message
function.description: Open a text message pre-filled with your recipient and body. IMPORTANT: this does NOT send the message. iOS requires the user to tap send in the sheet that appears, and there is no way for an app to bypass that. Report it as drafted, never as sent, unless the result says the user sent it.

to.description: Phone number, contact name, or saved nickname.

body.description: The message text, written in the user's voice.

function.name: place_call
function.description: Start a phone call. iOS shows a confirmation and then leaves Conduit for the Phone app. You cannot answer, decline or hang up calls; only start one.

to.description: Phone number, contact name, or saved nickname.

facetime.description: Use FaceTime instead of a cellular call.

function.name: send_email
function.description: Open an email pre-filled with recipients, subject and body. IMPORTANT: this does NOT send the email; the user must tap send in the sheet. You also cannot read the user's inbox - iOS gives apps no access to received mail.

to.description: Recipient email, contact name, or nickname. Separate several recipients with commas.

body.description: The email body, written in the user's voice.

function.name: create_event
function.description: Add an event to the user's calendar. This happens immediately with no confirmation once calendar access is granted.

start.description: Start time in local ISO 8601, for example 2026-09-16T15:30:00. Call get_current_time first if you need to work out a relative time.

end.description: End time in local ISO 8601. Omit to use duration_minutes instead.

duration_minutes.description: Length in minutes when end is not given. Defaults to 60.

alarm_minutes_before.description: Add an alert this many minutes before the start.

function.name: find_events
function.description: List calendar events in a time range. Use this to answer questions about the user's schedule and before scheduling anything, so you do not double-book.

query.description: Only return events whose title or location contains this.

function.name: check_availability
function.description: Check whether the user is free in a time range. Returns any conflicting events. Prefer this over find_events when the question is simply free or busy.

function.name: delete_event
function.description: Delete a calendar event by its id. Get ids from find_events. Deletes immediately. If several events could match, delete only the one the user meant.

function.name: create_reminder
function.description: Add a reminder to the user's Reminders list. Immediate, no confirmation.

due.description: When it is due, in local ISO 8601.

function.name: find_reminders
function.description: List the user's incomplete reminders, so you can answer what is on their list.

function.name: complete_reminder
function.description: Mark a reminder as done. Get ids from find_reminders.

function.name: schedule_notification
function.description: Schedule a local notification from Conduit at a specific time. Use this for nudges that are not really calendar events, such as reminding the user to call someone back in an hour.

at.description: When to fire, in local ISO 8601.

function.name: run_shortcut
function.description: Run one of the user's shortcuts from the Shortcuts app by name. This is how you reach things iOS does not expose to apps directly: setting an alarm, toggling a Focus mode, controlling smart home devices, changing settings. The shortcut must already exist on the device and the name must match exactly. This leaves Conduit and switches to Shortcuts.

name.description: The exact name of the existing shortcut.

input.description: Text to pass into the shortcut as its input.

function.name: open_app
function.description: Open another app on the phone, optionally with a search term. This switches away from Conduit.

function.name: get_directions
function.description: Open Maps with directions between two places. Copy each address exactly as the user gave it, including the street number, town or suburb and postcode. Leave origin out to start from the user's current location.

destination.description: Where to go: the full address or place name, including the town.

origin.description: Where to start: the full address including the town. Omit to start from the current location.

function.name: play_music
function.description: Open Music and search for something to play.

query.description: Artist, album, song or playlist to look for.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Open a web search in the browser. This leaves Conduit. Only call it when the user asks you to search the web or look something up online. Never call it to answer a question; answer from what you know instead.

function.name: copy_to_clipboard
function.description: Put text on the clipboard so the user can paste it anywhere. Useful when no tool can complete a task directly: prepare the text and let the user paste it.

function.name: run_javascript
function.description: Run JavaScript in a sandbox on this phone. Returns the value of the last expression and anything printed with console.log. Use it for any arithmetic beyond the trivial, percentages, unit and date calculations, and to test code you have written before giving it to the user. No network, no files, 10 second limit. Use BigInt (123n) for integers larger than 2^53.

code.description: JavaScript source. The final expression is the returned value.
